Last Friday (the 21st), on the day of the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, police took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing into custody in a police van during the early hours. Police responded to inquiries stating that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

Around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the queue, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue "appeared to have something slightly seditious about her clothing" and took her away in a police van. While officers removed the woman, several officers repeatedly directed reporters to leave, saying "we're taking you to the press area," and extended the orange cordon line toward Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police van, they put away the cordon line. On the day, a "court-watching volunteer" who had been queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese text printed on it.

The Collective spoke to police to ask why the woman was taken away and whether she had been arrested. Police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation around the West Kowloon Court on August 21, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
